### J-1 Nothing says how a human is told from an agent at the approve call
- quote: "WHEN anyone other than the human tries to approve the `pr` gate THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it"
- quote: "nio can't tell sessions apart, so independence comes from the unit, not from refusing an identity"
- situation (adversary): a building or fresh agent runs the approve command. The system "can't tell sessions apart", yet FR-9 and the decision table rows "building agent" and "fresh agent" must refuse it while "human" is accepted. No mechanism or signal is given for the human. AC-11 covers only "auto flag is on", and no AC covers an agent approving with the flag off. The refusal can be a no-op, or it can be bypassed by an agent that borrows the human's invocation form.
- situation (testability): the Decisions say nio cannot tell sessions apart, and the decision table has rows for "building agent" and "fresh agent", which are indistinguishable to the code. AC-11 only covers an agent with the auto flag on and an approved verdict. A test cannot say what makes a caller the human (the `--human` flag? a TTY?). The rows "fresh agent / off" and "building agent" have no AC. A tester could not write a test that fails if the building agent were let through.
- fix: name what makes an approval the human's (for example an explicit human-only flag or a pending-approval file), and add an AC where an agent approves with auto off.
- validation: confirmed: FR-9 and the decision table must tell the human from an agent, but the Decisions say "nio can't tell sessions apart". No signal for the human is named, and AC-11 covers only auto on with an approved verdict.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: approval only through a human-only command, no unruled finding, verdict not stale; merge records nothing; tables aligned (FR-9, AC-11, AC-21, AC-22, AC-23, AC-12)

### J-2 Push, PR creation and the comment have no failure or replay behaviour
- quote: "push the branch and open the pull request, have the gate's fresh driver post one comment"
- situation (adversary): the push is rejected, `gh` is missing or unauthenticated, or a pull request already exists for the branch. The comment post times out and is retried, or the driver restarts after the comment was posted. The spec doesn't say whether the effort stays at the gate silently with no pull request, opens a second pull request, or posts two verdict comments. "one comment" also conflicts with fix-check rounds, which each produce a new verdict. The human may then read a missing or stale verdict as "no findings".
- situation (testability): FR-16 depends on a remote, a push and `gh`. There is no AC for a failed push, no `gh` or auth, an already-open pull request for the branch, or a comment post that fails. A second run could post a second comment against "one comment". AC-7, AC-8 and AC-9 run a real model at e2e level, and a model is not deterministic. A run that happened to raise nothing, or a spurious extra finding, fails the test with no defect. FR-6 also names "needless complexity" and "cross-epic mismatch" and no AC covers either (AC-9 only tests their absence).
- fix: say what happens on each failure (the gate stays blocked and says so loudly), make the open and the comment idempotent, and say which comment is current after later rounds.
- validation: confirmed: FR-16 and AC-19 describe only the happy path (push, open, one comment). Nothing settles a rejected push, missing `gh`, an existing pull request, or a retried or replayed comment.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: reuse open PR; one verdict comment edited each round; failed push/PR/comment stops with message; e2e lens ACs pass 2 of 3 on a fixture (FR-16, AC-24, AC-25, AC-7..9)

### J-3 The verdict isn't tied to a commit, and a merge by an agent has no AC that contains it
- quote: "Misuse: the building orchestrator drives the `pr` gate itself, or an agent approves the gate or merges the pull request."
- quote: "Observable: `gh pr view` shows the open pull request and the comment; the branch is unmerged"
- situation (adversary): after `APPROVED` is posted, a commit lands on the branch: a hand fix, a merge resolution, or a push from the orchestrator. The comment now describes a diff that no longer exists, and the human merges on it. FR-3 judges the diff "when the packs are built", and nothing fixes which commit that was. The merge half of the misuse line is covered only by "nio merges no pull request" (SC-2). Nothing rejects or contains an agent running `gh pr merge`, and AC-19 only checks the branch is unmerged at one moment. If the pull request is merged while the gate is open, the state is undefined.
- fix: put the judged head SHA in the verdict comment and the ledger, treat a later commit as a stale verdict, and say what a merge before the gate closes does.
- validation: confirmed: FR-3 says only "when the packs are built". Neither the Verdict comment entity nor AC-19 ties the verdict to a head commit. The UJ-1 misuse line about an agent merging is backed only by SC-2 "nio merges no pull request", so a merge before the gate closes is undefined.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: verdict names the head commit judged; stale if HEAD moves (FR-16, AC-19, AC-26)

### J-4 In-flight efforts with open findings on an epic can lose them silently
- quote: "its closed gates stay closed, its remaining epics close on the suite alone"
- situation (adversary): an in-flight effort has an epic whose gate is mid-round, or at the cap with confirmed blockers, or has open fix tasks, when this lands. "close on the suite alone" lets the epic close and drops those findings. The `pr` gate then judges a fresh diff that may not re-raise them. AC-15 tests only the case where gates are already closed and E-2 is "in progress".
- fix: say what becomes of open epic findings and open ledgers (carried into the `pr` gate, or blocking the switch), and add an AC.
- validation: confirmed: FR-12 and AC-15 cover closed gates and E-2 "in progress". Epics with a mid-round gate, capped open findings or open fix tasks are not addressed, and "close on the suite alone" would drop them.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: part-way epic closes on the new rule; an epic already in its old jury finishes it first (FR-12, AC-15, AC-28, Decisions)

### J-5 An epic can close on a missing or vacuous suite
- quote: "close the epic only when the whole test suite passes, with no reviewers and no rounds"
- situation (adversary): the project has no configured suite, the suite collects zero tests, or the builder skips or deletes failing tests to make it pass. Every epic then closes silently on an empty "pass". Removing the per-epic jury also removes the only per-epic check for weakened tests, and the single `pr` gate sees them only at the end. The Decisions section says evidence is reused "only when it ran the configured suite and passed", but FR-1 doesn't require a configured suite or a non-empty run.
- fix: say that no configured suite, or zero tests run, refuses the epic close, and note that the `pr` gate looks for tampering with tests.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q8: moot; epics no longer close on the whole suite, which runs once at the pr gate

### J-11 One verdict comment, but the gate runs several rounds
- quote: "holds one comment from the gate's driver whose first word is `APPROVED` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`"
- quote: "round ends with confirmed blocker, below cap (fix tasks in `PR fixes`, next round)"
- situation (logic): Round 1 ends with a confirmed blocker, so the verdict is `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and the state table row `pr gate` has the verdict posted. Fix tasks are built and round 2 (the fix check) ends `APPROVED`. FR-16 and AC-19 allow one comment, so either the first verdict is never posted, or the second verdict can't be posted, or the PR holds two comments. The spec doesn't say which.
- fix: say whether the comment is posted once at the end of the gate or once per round, and whether a later comment replaces or edits the earlier one.
- validation: confirmed: FR-16, AC-19 and the Verdict comment entity say "one comment". FR-7 and the state table have a REQUEST_CHANGES round followed by a fix check, so a later verdict has no stated place. The spec doesn't say whether the comment is posted once at the end or per round.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: reuse open PR; one verdict comment edited each round; failed push/PR/comment stops with message; e2e lens ACs pass 2 of 3 on a fixture (FR-16, AC-24, AC-25, AC-7..9)

### J-12 Out-of-flow commits can fall outside every split pack
- quote: "each requirement-checking lens one epic's diff per juror"
- quote: "A change committed outside the flow on the effort's branch is always inside the judged diff."
- situation (logic): The diff is over 1,500 lines and a hand fix or merge resolution touches a file. The requirement lenses get one pack per epic, and the commit belongs to no epic, so no pack holds it. Only the integration lens sees it, and only at "summary level". AC-3 and SC-3 are then false for exactly the large efforts. The same gap applies to a `PR fixes` epic, if it counts as an epic for packing.
- situation (testability): an effort over 1,500 lines contains a hand-fix commit (AC-3) or a `PR fixes` epic task, and neither belongs to an epic the packs are split by. A test cannot say which pack holds that diff, so the split may silently drop it and break SC-3. Also, only the over-the-limit case is tested. There is no AC at or just under `jury.split_lines`, and no AC for how "summary level" is told apart from a full pack, so nothing fails if the integration lens gets the whole raw diff.
- fix: state which pack holds out-of-flow changes, for example an extra pack for non-epic commits, and whether `PR fixes` has its own pack.
- validation: confirmed: FR-13 and AC-17 give each requirement lens "one epic's diff". An out-of-flow commit belongs to no epic, so no pack holds it, while AC-3 and SC-3 say it is always judged. The spec doesn't say whether `PR fixes` has its own pack.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: commits outside any epic, PR fixes included, get one extra pack (FR-13, AC-17, AC-27)

### J-13 The human's approval is unconditional in one table and conditional in the other
- quote: "gate closes when no finding is unruled"
- quote: "approves by merging or recording the gate"
- situation (logic): In the state table row `pr gate`, "human approves the gate" always gives "→ done". The decision table only closes the gate when no finding is unruled. If the human records approval while a finding is open, the two tables give different outcomes. The summary also lets the human approve "by merging", but no state row or transition handles a merge, and SC-2 needs approval of the gate before `done`. A merge made without recording the gate has no defined outcome.
- fix: put the "no unruled finding" condition in the state table cell, and say how a merge by the human moves the gate to `done`.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: approval only through a human-only command, no unruled finding, verdict not stale; merge records nothing; tables aligned (FR-9, AC-11, AC-21, AC-22, AC-23, AC-12)

### J-14 Fix tasks re-trigger the transition to the pr gate
- quote: "WHEN every task of every epic, fix tasks included, is done THE SYSTEM SHALL move the effort to one `pr` jury gate"
- quote: "→ pr gate | ignore | ignore | → pr gate | → pr gate | → pr gate"
- situation (logic): The effort is at the `pr gate` and fix tasks are created in `PR fixes`. FR-2 says the effort moves to the pr gate when all tasks are done, and FR-1 says a closing epic goes on to the next epic. The state table has no row for fix tasks being built. `pr gate` is shown as unchanged, while `implementing` is the only row where tasks are built, and its "last task of last epic done" column says "pull request opened". - fix: add a state, or a note on the `pr gate` row, saying that fix-task completion goes to the fix check, not to a new pull request or a new gate.
- validation: ungrounded: a cited ID or quote is not in the artefact

C-261030-abpr (accepted) is a build-order fix against the old effort's task plan (it moves T-4 and T-27), not a spec rule that binds this spec. AC-1 already fixes the observable: `nio flow status` names E-2's next task after E-1 closes on the suite.

### J-23 Epic closes on the suite alone, against current decision D-261106-ltsr
- quote: "close the epic only when the whole test suite passes"
- quote: "An epic closes only when the whole suite passes; no reviewers, no rounds"
- situation (consistency): D-261106-ltsr (current) says the epic check runs the implement-stage tests and the full suite only at the end. A builder following FR-1 runs the full suite at the end of every epic, which the current decision forbids. No change request against D-261106-ltsr is cited, so the requirement goes against a current decision without one.
- fix: either write a change request against D-261106-ltsr and cite it in FR-1 and the Decisions line, or keep the epic check on the implement-stage tests and move the full suite to the end.
- validation: merged: same as J-6

### J-24 In-flight efforts: "next epic" versus "E-2 closes on the suite alone"
- quote: "Efforts already implementing switch at their next epic"
- quote: "check E-2 closes on the suite alone"
- situation (consistency): an effort has E-1's gate approved and E-2 in progress when this lands. Under the Decisions line, the switch happens at E-2's next epic, so E-2 would still be judged by a jury. Under US-4 and AC-15, E-2 closes on the suite alone. The builder cannot tell which applies to the epic already in progress.
- fix: say whether an epic already in progress closes on the suite alone, and make the Decisions line and US-4 match.
- validation: confirmed: The Decisions line says in-flight efforts "switch at their next epic", while US-4's independent test and AC-15 say E-2, already in progress, closes on the suite alone. FR-12 says "remaining epics". Nothing settles whether the epic already in progress counts as remaining or as the one before the switch.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Q9: part-way epic closes on the new rule; an epic already in its old jury finishes it first (FR-12, AC-15, AC-28, Decisions)

### J-25 Accepted epic-line rule (C-261030-abpr) is not carried into the new epic close
- quote: "no `implementation-E-1` ledger or pack exists"
- situation (consistency): C-261030-abpr (accepted) says `nio flow done implementation-E-n` writes the epic line and CT-17 says claim refuses the next epic until that line exists. The spec removes the implementation gates but never says what writes the epic line on a suite-only close, or whether the claim check still applies. If CT-17 stays, the next epic is refused; if it goes, the accepted change is dropped without a change request. The spec does not say which. (Inferred from the pack's memory items, not from code.)
- fix: state what records the suite-only epic close and whether CT-17 still holds, or raise a change request against C-261030-abpr.
- validation: refuted: It is the same point as J-8 and J-22. The epic line is HOW, and C-261030-abpr is a build-order change against another effort's plan. AC-1 and FR-1 give the observable: `nio flow status` names the next epic's task. The spec need not say what writes an internal line. The finding itself says it is inferred, not read from the spec or code.

### J-26 Undefined setting `jury.max_runs` next to `jury.max_rounds`
- quote: "The `pr` gate's own default `jury.max_runs` is 7"
- quote: "the round cap `jury.max_rounds`"
- situation (consistency): FR-7 caps the rounds with `jury.max_rounds`, while the Decisions section sets a default for `jury.max_runs` of 7 and gives it no definition. A reader cannot tell whether `jury.max_runs` caps rounds, lens runs, or something else, so the cap the driver enforces is unclear.
- fix: define `jury.max_runs` in one place, state how it differs from `jury.max_rounds`, or use one name.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Decisions: jury.max_runs defined as the existing cap on lens runs per gate (each juror counted), distinct from the round cap jury.max_rounds

### J-27 "closing task's review" versus "no reviewers"
- quote: "the closing task's review ran the full suite"
- quote: "with no reviewers and no rounds"
- situation (consistency): FR-1 says the epic closes with no reviewers, yet AC-1 and AC-16 check a review on the closing task that runs the suite and names failing tests. A reader cannot tell whether the closing task has a review step or whether "review" just means the suite run.
- fix: name the thing the closing task produces (for example, the suite run and its result) and drop "review" from AC-1 and AC-16, or say what the review is.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: AC-1/AC-16: 'the closing task's review' now reads 'review step (its suite run)', so it is not a juror review
